extracted.intended_audience: media scholars, journalism researchers, and journalists interested in news framing and newsworthiness
extracted.subtask_description: Apply Entman's framing model to assess or produce news coverage by identifying which aspects of an event are made salient to promote a problem definition, causal interpretation, moral evaluation, and/or treatment recommendation, and by locating frames in communicator, text, receiver, and culture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Framing definition
rubrics_metrics.description: "To frame is to select some aspects of a perceived reality and make them more salient in a communicating text, in such a way as to promote a particular problem definition, causal interpretation, moral evaluation, and/or treatment recommendation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This canonical definition captures both the selection and salience functions of framing and ties framing directly to promoting one or more interpretive outcomes (problem definition, cause, moral judgment, remedy). Use this as the core test: does the text make particular aspects more noticeable/meaningful/memorable to promote one of the four functions?

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem Definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying what the issue is — naming the event as a problem (e.g., "drug epidemic," "border crisis," "housing shortage").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsworthiness increases when an event can be cleanly labeled as a problem. Evaluate whether the story offers a clear, concise label or definition that organizes the facts into an issue; lack of a clear problem-definition makes events harder to cover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Causal Interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Explaining what causes the problem; attributing responsibility to a person, policy, or specific factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events with attributable causes outrank those with diffuse causation. Assess whether the text links the problem to identifiable causes or agents and whether it presents competing causal accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral Evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessing right/wrong or good/bad — assigning moral judgments such as identifying a villain, victim, or hero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories that license clear moral judgment fit the framing form better than morally ambiguous events. Check for evaluative language, characterizations, and moral positioning that guide audience judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment Recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggesting remedies or courses of action (e.g., legislation, donations, individual choices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events tied to actionable solutions gain coverage incentive. Determine whether the coverage links the problem to concrete responses and whether those responses are presented as feasible or desirable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicator locus
rubrics_metrics.description: Frames stem from journalists' beliefs about the audience, the source, and the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider journalist-oriented factors (assumptions about audience preferences, source selection, institutional constraints) that shape which frames are produced and emphasized. Reviewer/producer should inspect reporter/editor intent and sourcing strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Text locus
rubrics_metrics.description: Frames are realized through keywords, metaphors, sources cited, image choice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze textual affordances: which words, images, metaphors, selection of experts/sources, headlines, and story structure make aspects more salient? Coding or content analysis should capture these textual devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiver locus
rubrics_metrics.description: Audiences may decode frames differently than intended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for audience interpretation variance: reception studies should check how different audiences construe the frame and whether decoding aligns with the communicator's intended frame.

rubrics_metrics.name: Culture locus
rubrics_metrics.description: Common stock of frames in a society shapes which framings are publicly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate how culturally available frame templates (e.g., crime, terrorism, scandal) constrain or enable particular framings. Novel issues lacking cultural templates will be harder to frame and thus harder to cover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame-availability as a news value
rubrics_metrics.description: An event must be reducible to one or more of the four functions for it to be reportable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reducibility to the four functions as an implicit newsworthiness criterion: if a story can be given a clear problem definition, cause, moral evaluation, or remedy, it is more likely to be picked up; absence of these makes coverage less likely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salience selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Framing increases the salience of selected aspects — making them 'more noticeable, meaningful, or memorable.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how framing choices make certain facts or actors more prominent. News selection and frame selection are inseparable: examine which elements are foregrounded or backgrounded to judge influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predictive use: cultural frame mapping
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues that map onto culturally available frames (e.g., crime, terrorism, scandal) become newsworthy faster than novel issues that lack a frame template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply this as a predictive criterion: identify whether an issue fits existing cultural templates to estimate coverage likelihood and speed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frame contestation as news generator
rubrics_metrics.description: When competing frames vie over an event (e.g., 'freedom fighter' vs. 'terrorist'), the dispute itself becomes news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for situations with multiple competing framings; the presence of an active frame contest often sustains continued coverage. Treat contestation as a distinct newsworthiness signal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mechanism linking cognition, text, and news values
rubrics_metrics.description: Frames operate at the intersection of journalist cognition, text affordances, and audience interpretation — explaining why news values like personalization and unambiguity work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this integrative mechanism as analytic guidance: evaluate how cognitive tendencies of journalists and audiences, together with textual devices, produce observable news values and selection patterns.
